title: Chapter 25: Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI)

blocks.content: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is the statutory body responsible for regulating the telecommunications sector in India. It ensures fair competition, protects consumer interests, and promotes orderly growth of telecom services.
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) is the statutory body responsible for regulating the telecommunications sector in India.

items: Remember that TRAI is a statutory body regulating the telecommunications sector.
Competitive exam questions often test TRAI's primary mandates: fair competition, consumer protection, and orderly telecom growth.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI serves as the statutory regulatory authority for the telecom sector in India.
It is responsible for maintaining fair competition among telecom operators.
Consumer interest protection is a key objective of TRAI's regulatory framework.
TRAI facilitates and promotes the orderly growth of telecommunication services nationwide.
